fields.name: National Engineering Case Competition
fields.case_title: Reduce energy usage in your community
fields.case_description:
As a team you will define the community, the baseline, and scope (campus building, a neighborhood, a process, a system, etc.).

A competitive response will consider the following:

  • Scope. Define a specific problem with a quantified baseline you can measure against.
  • Analysis. Show engineering work such as calculations, modeling, data, or trade studies.
  • Development. Address cost, schedule, and other constraints to utilize the $400 grant to prototype or demonstrate.
  • Metrics. Tie specific, measurable success metrics back to the case objective.
fields.about:
Purpose

  • Engineering In Action. Take an open-ended, real-world problem from research and analysis through design, build, and measured results.
  • Skills Members Can Show. Trade studies, feasibility analysis, budgeting, technical writing, and project execution is work every member of the team can utilize in their career.
  • A Portfolio For Your Chapter. Finalist work is funded, built, and documented, giving your chapter a visible engineering project on campus and in your community.
  • Recognition For Technical Work. This national award recognizes what your members can build, showcased as part of the entire Theta Tau professional community.
  • Connection Across Theta Tau. Every chapter works the same case in the same semester, creating a shared challenge and friendly competition across regions.

Timeline

  1. Case Released (September 2026). Every chapter receives the engineering case, the rubric, and submission requirements.
  2. Chapter Proposal (fall semester). Your chapter has the semester to research the case and write a proposal.
  3. Regional Qualifiers (January 2027). Up to two qualifying proposals per region advance to the development phase.
  4. Funded Build (spring semester). Each qualifying chapter receives $400 to prototype, pilot, or otherwise develop the idea.
  5. National Winners (Convention 2027). Finalists are showcased; first and second place earn chapter dues awards.

Awards

  • First place: dues reduction. The national first-place chapter has its chapter dues reduced for the following academic year.
  • Second place: dues reduction. The national second-place chapter receives a smaller dues reduction, also applied the following year.
  • $400 Development Grant. Awarded to each regional qualifying chapter to prototype, pilot, or build. Up to 20 chapters funded this cycle.

fields.name: Final submission
fields.instructions: Additional information will be provided to qualifying chapters.

fields.name: Problem Definition & Research
fields.description: Problem is precisely scoped with a quantified baseline. Research draws on credible technical sources and, where relevant, stakeholder or user input. Assumptions are explicit and justified.

fields.name: Technical Rigor & Analysis
fields.description: Sound engineering fundamentals applied throughout. Calculations, modeling, or data analysis are correct, appropriately detailed, and clearly documented. Trade studies compare alternatives against quantified criteria.

fields.name: Solution Design & Feasibility
fields.description: Design is complete and practical. Constraints (cost, schedule, safety, regulatory) are identified and addressed. A realistic implementation path and budget show the idea could be executed with the $400 grant or a clearly justified plan beyond it.

fields.name: Impact & Measurability
fields.description: Projected impact is quantified against the baseline with well-considered estimates. Success metrics are specific, measurable, and tied to the case objective.

fields.name: Innovation & Creativity
fields.description: Approach is original or applies existing technology in a novel, well-justified way that clearly improves on standard solutions.

fields.name: Communication & Professionalism
fields.description: Proposal is well organized, concise, and polished. Figures, tables, and citations are professional and support the argument. Accessible to a technical reviewer from any discipline.

fields.name: Team & Chapter Engagement
fields.description: Documented participation drawing from multiple disciplines and class years, with clearly defined roles.

fields.name: Execution of Development Plan
fields.description: The chapter substantially executed its proposed plan within the grant period, adapting thoughtfully where reality diverged from the proposal. Grant spending is fully documented and well justified.

fields.name: Demonstrated Results
fields.description: Results are measured against the metrics proposed in Phase 1 and honestly reported, including shortfalls. Evidence (data, prototype performance, pilot outcomes) is credible and verifiable.

fields.name: Technical Learning & Iteration
fields.description: Final report shows rigorous engineering judgment: failures analyzed, design iterated, and conclusions supported by evidence gathered during development.

fields.name: Sustainability & Path Forward
fields.description: Clear, realistic plan for continuing, scaling, or handing off the project beyond the competition, including resources required.

fields.name: Final Presentation & Report Quality
fields.description: Final report and presentation are polished, well organized, and communicate the work compellingly to a multidisciplinary audience.

fields.label: Proposal
fields.description: Your proposal as a PDF or PowerPoint file, 10 to 20 slides. PDF is recommended. Link to any video instead of putting it in the file.

fields.label: Final report
fields.description: Your final report as a PDF.

fields.label: Final presentation
fields.description: Your final presentation as a PDF or PowerPoint file.

fields.label: Grant spending summary
fields.description: How the $400 grant was spent, with the receipts, as a PDF or a spreadsheet.

fields.label: Video
fields.description: Optional: a link to a video of the project, such as on YouTube or Google Drive.
